Expressions are field references (nested paths included), &#95;&#95;name&#95;&#95;, literals, the six comparisons, array and map construction and document&#95;id / collection&#95;id / parent of a document reference. FS-ENT-ORACLE O-1 (production, Enterprise, 2026-10-19) answered every comparison, construction, alias and where-condition probe as the official emulator does, so both profiles answer them alike: comparisons follow one order (missing operands, null, NaN, kinds that differ, the integer and double boundaries, arrays and maps included), a where keeps a row only when its condition is true, array(...) writes null for a missing element, map(...) leaves out a missing value, and select aliases are field paths. What production has not answered (collection&#95;id or parent of a missing, null or non-reference value, collection&#95;id of the documents root, repeated or non-string map keys, literals holding expressions other than a map holding a field, a constant where condition) is refused at run time with UNIMPLEMENTED under strict and answered as the official emulator answers it under the emulator profile. A field equality is applied by the scan without index validation (Enterprise needs no index; pending production observation). A run-time refusal may follow partial results; rows after a used-up limit are not evaluated. The same subset runs over REST :executePipeline (the Web SDK Lite transport); a REST refusal answers no partial results. Without a select a result is the whole source document (name and times); every response carries the snapshot read time as executionTime. Known differences from production: results without a sort come in another order than document names, and production puts all results of a small answer in one response or array element. Offset skips filtered rows once across the existing paged stream. The official emulator's 64-field select limit is not applied. All other functions/stages, logical operators and consistency selectors remain unsupported.
